finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id deletes any project regardless of ownership because the result of authorized() is discarded, so any caller who can reach the route can delete another user's project by id.
finding.source: req.params.id on DELETE /projects/:id (api.js:16-17), with the caller needing to be authenticated (auth middleware not in this directory, so assumed).

trace.note: project = req.store.projects.get(req.params.id) with no owner scope
authorized(req.user, project) called as a bare statement; boolean return value ignored
authorized() helper returns ownerId === user.id || isAdmin === true but never throws, so it cannot enforce anything when its result is unused

finding.guards_checked: No if/throw wraps the call at api.js:18. The sibling PUT /projects/:id/name handler (api.js:25) uses authorize(), which throws on failure, so that route is enforced; the DELETE route is not. Authentication middleware, req.store/req.user setup and error handler are not in this directory and were not verified.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. The only check is authorized() at api.js:18, which returns a boolean (api.js:12-14) and is called as a bare statement, so its result is discarded. The throwing helper authorize() (api.js:4-10) is not called on this route. The PUT route at api.js:25 does use authorize(), so the gap is specific to DELETE.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: api.js:18 discards the boolean from authorized() (api.js:12-14), and api.js:19 deletes project.id unconditionally, so any caller who reaches the route can delete another owner's project. The attacker only needs whatever authentication the route requires, and the auth middleware is outside this directory, so the attacker's required role is unverified.
